findings.title: Three.js game prototype from one prompt
findings.summary: The author linked a generated cat-and-mouse game and reported about 40 minutes for the run.
findings.conditions: Fable 5.2 at Extra effort. One prompt, with a link to the generated game.

findings.title: Ported a Three.js scene to WebGL
findings.summary: The author got a working vanilla JavaScript port whose rendering differed from the original. The comment links both demos and the transcript.
findings.conditions: Opus 5.5 at Medium effort in the same Claude Chat thread that built the original. The author compared the results visually.

findings.title: SVG drawings at three effort levels
findings.summary: The author shared three pelican drawings, judged even the low-effort result favourably, and reported costs of roughly US$0.10 to US$0.17 per drawing.
findings.conditions: Gemini 4 Argon at low, medium and high reasoning effort. One drawing prompt and a subjective comparison.

findings.title: Photo ranking changed with attachment order
findings.summary: The author could not find a prompt that kept the photo choice consistent when they reordered the attachments.
findings.conditions: One informal experiment with multiple images in GPT-6 Astra Decisions.

findings.title: Max effort ran out of tokens before returning an SVG
findings.summary: The author reported about 15 minutes and 128,000 thinking tokens before the run ended without a final drawing. The comment gives results for the other effort levels.
findings.conditions: Sonnet 5.5 at maximum thinking effort on one pelican-drawing prompt.

findings.title: Ported model inference to run in the browser
findings.summary: The author got an interactive ONNX demo running with help from Opus 4.8 and shared the demo, code and agent transcript.
findings.conditions: Claude Code and one ONNX port. The demo download was about 1.3 GB.

findings.title: Reports fewer shortcuts around tests with newer Claude releases
findings.summary: The author said Claude 3.7 and 4 took fewer shortcuts to make tests pass in their work. When it still happened, they had the agent undo the shortcut and fix the underlying problem.
findings.conditions: Informal comparison across releases. The comment gives no task list or counts.

findings.title: Keep questions and results in the coordinating thread
findings.summary: The author starts tasks in a Project and lets delegated threads do their work while the main thread collects questions and results.
findings.conditions: The author described less context switching in their Claude Code Projects workflow.

findings.title: Prototype several uses of a proposed API
findings.summary: The author uses coding agents to build disposable clients that exercise an API in different ways before committing to its design.
findings.conditions: A design practice for APIs still in flux, based on the author's own use.

findings.title: Verify fixes against a protected copy of the tests
findings.summary: Run acceptance checks against a reserved test suite when an agent could make the working tests pass by editing them.
findings.conditions: The advice addresses regressions checked by an existing test suite.

findings.title: Give parallel agents a shared place for findings
findings.summary: The author suggests having research agents read prior findings and post their own in the same format in a shared GitHub Discussion.
findings.conditions: The source links one agent report and proposes the workflow for additional workers.

findings.title: Confirm the test command works before editing
findings.summary: The author starts coding sessions with a test run to verify the agent can execute the suite. They recommend having the agent test its edits as it goes.
findings.conditions: The author's example uses pytest in a project with tests already in place.

findings.title: Search the codebase and save plans to files
findings.summary: The author uses code search and file-based plans as examples of how coding agents can work across a repository larger than a single context window.
findings.conditions: This relies on agents having search and file access. The source compares context sizes using Codex and Claude as examples.
